PullRequest.Title: Keep the new tab button next to the last tab when tabs wrap
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349040

When editor tabs wrap, the add tab (+) button at the end of the tabs can end up alone on the last row, although the last tab would fit next to it. A row holding only the "+" looks like an empty tab row. This PR keeps the "+" next to the last tab.

**Before:** the "+" alone on the last row.

![Wrapped tabs with the + button alone on the last row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/496c574a-52b4-442f-ab97-71abccd43174)

**After:** the last tab moves down next to the "+".

![Wrapped tabs with the last tab and the + button on the last row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cae9a57-c4fd-4931-94ea-39a966ba68f1)

(Code OSS from this branch, Default Dark Modern, `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` and `workbench.editor.newTabButton` on. The "before" image is the same window with the new behavior switched off, which is the layout of `main`.)

## What changes

- After the wrapping layout, if the "+" ended up alone on the last row, `MultiEditorTabsControl` adds an `add-tab-follows-last-tab` class to the tab strip. The last tab then reserves the space of the "+" and the editor toolbar in its end margin, which moves it down to the row of the "+", and the "+" overlaps that margin with a matching negative start margin. The previous tab becomes the last in its row.
- This only applies when the last tab, the "+" and the editor toolbar fit on one row. Fit tabs of the modern UI may shrink to their minimum width (80px) for this, as their existing maximum width already allows. The class is reverted if the "+" still does not end up on the last tab's row. Otherwise, as in very narrow editor groups, the "+" keeps its own row as before.
- The wrapping decision itself is unchanged: the class is removed before it, so it measures the tabs as before. This matters because wrapping keeps its state between layouts.
- Applies to the classic and the modern tab styles, in the workbench and in the Agents window.

@chryw: this changes the "+ alone on the last row" layout you made consistent in #341337 and #341897. That layout remains the fallback when the last tab does not fit, and its alignment is still covered by the tests. Happy to adjust if the controls-only row was meant as a design choice rather than a fallback.

## Also: pressing the "+" again while its menu is open

While the menu of the "+" is open, pressing the "+" again picks its default (most recent) entry. Two problems with that:

- A press near the left edge of the "+" did nothing; only the center worked. In the Connected tab style the button's label has a -5px start margin, so the visible button extends beyond the `.tabs-bar-add-tab` element. The second-press hit test only used that element's bounds, and presses on those 5px fell through to the context menu's full-window mouse block (`.context-view-block`), which swallows mousedown. `EditorAddTabControl` now hit-tests the label's bounds too.
- The cursor turned into an arrow over the "+" while the menu was open, although it can still be clicked: the mouse block sets `cursor: initial`. While the pointer is over the "+", the block now shows a pointer cursor.

## Component fixtures

New `editor/tabs/NewTabButton` fixtures render four wrapped tabs with the "+" and assert the layout: `WrappedConnected`, `WrappedPill` and `WrappedLegacy` (the "+" follows the last tab) and `WrappedTooNarrow` (170px, the "+" keeps its own row). In the existing Agents window fixture `sessions/editorHeader/WrappedEditorActions` the last tab now shares the row with the "+", so its screenshot baseline changes; `ControlsOnlyLastRow` (180px) is unchanged.

## Also: recent-first menu as an explicit option

Only the workbench "+" lists the entry picked last first and picks it on a second press. This used to be keyed on the workbench's menu ID; it is now an explicit editor group option, `tabsBarAddTabRecentFirst`, which the workbench editor part sets and the Agents window (and its chat windows) explicitly leave off. The placement of the "+" is the same in both windows (measured: button and hover fill size, 2px gap after the last tab, vertical center), wrapping or not.

## Also: drop indicator after the last tab

When dragging an editor after the last tab, no insertion indicator showed once the "+" was in the tab strip (the workbench with `workbench.editor.newTabButton`, and the Agents window):
- Over the empty part of the strip, the indicator went to the tab container's last child, which is the "+" rather than the last tab. It now goes to the last tab.
- Over the "+" itself, the drag was ignored, so dropping there did nothing. It now drops after the last tab, like the empty strip.
- Modern tabs hid the last tab's indicator, because a rule used `:last-child` to recognize the last tab; it now uses the `last-tab` class. Without wrapping, the sticky "+" also covered the indicator, so the last tab is raised above it while it is the drop target.

Checked live with and without the "+" and with and without wrapping, in the workbench and the Agents window; a test covers the drop target and the indicator's visibility.

**Before:** dragging a tab past the last tab (tabs not wrapping), no indicator before the "+".

![Dragging past the last tab without wrapping: no insertion indicator before the + button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97dec94a-8ad9-4eec-a5ba-c7bd004b6b25)

**After:** the indicator shows between the last tab and the "+".

![Dragging past the last tab: the insertion indicator shows between the last tab and the + button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fc67930-7bc4-460b-819d-9dcaa78069dd)

(Code OSS from this branch, Default Dark Modern, zoomed crops.)


## Also: "+" on a row of its own lines up with the tabs in the workbench

In groups too narrow for the last tab, the "+" and the editor toolbar on one row, the "+" keeps a row of its own (the `WrappedTooNarrow` fixture). The tabs control already computes an inset that aligns it with the leading tab of the row above, but only the Agents window's stylesheet applied it, so in the workbench the "+" sat at the very start of the row. Those rules moved from the Agents window's `editorPart.css` to the shared Modern UI tab styles, so both windows place it the same way. The existing Agents window alignment test now also runs without the Agents window classes, and at a width where the "+" is alone on its row.

**After:** in a 520px wide window, the "+" alone on the last row starts where the file icons of the tabs above start.

![Narrow workbench editor group: the + button alone on the last row lines up with the file icons of the tabs above](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce329f97-d286-48b3-825f-1bc31fc7ca84)


## Validation

- Workbench `src/tsconfig.json` type check with tsgo (dev-workspace `coreTypecheck`): passed.
- `node build/oxlint.ts` and `node build/stylelint.ts` on the changed files: passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editorTabsLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --browser chromium`: 117 passing. Tests that asserted the "+" alone on the last row now expect it next to the last tab when that fits, and the old layout otherwise; the "upper pills" test asserts that both cases are exercised. The wrapped fit check test derives the tab gutter from the last tab's margin, which now also holds the "+" and toolbar space.
- Manual, in Code OSS from this branch with nine wrapped tabs: resizing the window from 1500px to 520px in 3px steps, the "+" never overlapped the editor toolbar or left the tab strip, and it was alone on a row only where not even a minimum-width last tab fit beside it (modern style). The classic style only leaves the strip where tabs stop wrapping and scroll instead, as on `main`.
- The second-press test also presses the part of the label outside the control; it fails with the previous hit test. Verified live in Code OSS: pressing 2px from the left edge of the "+" opens the menu, pressing there again opens the default entry and closes the menu, and the cursor over the "+" is a pointer while the menu is open.
- The new fixtures render without errors in the Component Explorer and reach their asserted layouts.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed margin rules, both write/read flush points, callers, and per-control animation-frame coalescing are directly traceable. This is static evidence of extra work, not a measured frame-time result; its bounded and configuration-dependent magnitude warrants low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread browser style/flex layout work over the tab strip and an additional array/geometry pass over its tabs.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One undo-and-reapply cycle per affected visible tab control per scheduled animation frame, with layout and row-marker work scaling with that control's tab count; requests in the same frame are already coalesced.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional synchronous renderer CPU/layout time on the next-paint critical path, including warm updates with unchanged geometry.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing wrapping layout measured and updated row markers without temporarily changing the last tab's margins to move it between rows and then restoring that arrangement.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every queued tab layout now removes the follow class before measuring wrapping, then reapplies it and measures again when the button would otherwise be orphaned, including when tab and group geometry have not changed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added unconditional classList.remove at line 2139 changes the margins defined by the new add-tab-follows-last-tab CSS rules. doLayoutTabsWrapping immediately reads addTabContainer.offsetWidth at line 2249; the new helper reapplies the class at line 2419 and immediately reads offsetTop at line 2420.
Findings.Title: Preserve the follow layout on geometry-neutral updates
Findings.Impact: For groups containing many wrapped tabs, repeated tab activation or resizing spends additional renderer time laying out an intermediate arrangement that is never displayed, reducing frame headroom and input responsiveness.
Findings.Evidence: With wrapTabs enabled and the follow class already active, removing it moves the last tab back to the previous row. The subsequent geometry read flushes that intermediate flex layout, and layoutAddTabWithLastTab then changes the margins again and synchronously flushes the corrected layout. The helper also repeats the collection-wide row-marker measurement. This repeats for unchanged-size calls from handleOpenedEditors (including reopening the active editor), selection/dirty invalidation in Connected tabs, and group layout. layout() coalesces requests within one animation frame, but does not suppress these cycles across frames.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the existing follow/wrapping decision for geometry-neutral updates rather than always removing the class. Invalidate that decision when available/container dimensions, tab geometry or membership, toolbar width, or add-button visibility/width changes; retain the unadjusted measurement when such an invalidation actually requires it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore, activate, update, and resize wrapped editor tabs in classic, Pill, and Connected styles, in the workbench and Agents windows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tab layout runs synchronously in a scheduled animation-frame callback before the next paint. Its final height can trigger group relayout. The new follow correction runs after the existing wrapping measurement; narrow groups and nonwrapping/hidden-button cases return without applying it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style/flex layout flushed by offsetWidth/offsetTop/getComputedStyle reads after changing layout-affecting classes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per visible tabs control, at most one scheduled callback per animation frame. A previously followed layout is undone and synchronously measured, then reapplied and synchronously measured; successful correction adds a batched O(N) row-marker pass for N tabs. A failed correction performs only one attempted application and removal, not a retry loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing wrapping already measured geometry and row markers, but did not undo and restore a followed last-tab arrangement on each invocation. The additional margin-driven layout cycle and second row-marker pass are introduced here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer work consumes the animation-frame budget before paint. Multiple affected controls execute on the same renderer thread.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tabs per visible group/control and frequency of layout-triggering activation, dirty/selection updates, decoration/toolbar changes, and resizing; requests within a frame are coalesced, not multiplied by their raw count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending animation-frame callback per tabs control; synchronous execution on the shared renderer thread. Reads in the new row-marker pass are collected before class writes, avoiding per-tab read/write alternation there.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing used dimensions cache getHeight results, and the scheduler coalesces pending requests. Neither preserves the new follow decision across warm geometry-neutral layouts: the class is removed unconditionally. No filesystem, network, subprocess, database, or IPC work is reached by the changed layout calculation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed CSS margins, unconditional removal, both subsequent geometry-read sites, and layout callers establish the repeated warm layout mechanism directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Impact depends on wrapping/button settings, orphan-producing geometry, tab counts, affected group count, and hardware; the extra work is bounded, so the finding is low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one introduced synchronous-layout regression: geometry-neutral warm updates repeatedly undo and restore an already-correct follow arrangement. Necessary first-use fitting and bounded narrow-group fallback are not separately reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the workbench add-tab menu, move the pointer over its visible label, and press again to execute the default action; compare the Agents window's plain menu.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu rendering and hit testing run on the renderer thread. Mouse movement now performs a small label query, one or two rectangle reads, and a cursor assignment. A second press invokes the existing action runner; storage persistence and telemetry are not awaited before invoking the selected command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the button label, read at most two DOM rectangles, and update the menu mouse-block cursor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One helper invocation per captured mouse move outside the rendered menu and per captured mousedown while the menu is visible; one small button subtree, not all tabs or all groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hit testing read one control rectangle. Menu highlighting and its window mouse listeners already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous input-handler work. Existing code already read the control rectangle on these events; the diff adds the label fallback and local cursor styling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the recent command from profile storage and persist a newly picked command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reads are in-memory Map lookups. A changed command updates the existing per-menu key; unchanged values are deduplicated and persistence uses the existing throttled flush rather than one awaited database operation per event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workbench already enabled recent/default behavior by menu ID, and Agents did not. The explicit options preserve those choices and storage operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cached lookup is synchronous; persistence is off the menu-selection critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch existing opened/picked/dismissed telemetry through the configured appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing lifecycle events, not mouse-move events; small fixed-size payload containing menu ID and optional entry ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry lifecycle and payload existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No newly awaited telemetry boundary; downstream transport is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pointer-event frequency while one menu is open and the small contributed action collection. Added hit-test work does not scale with editor-tab count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial renderer event handling. Menu listeners exist only while visible. Existing throttled storage batching handles persistence; selecting an action still invokes it once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recent-entry storage reads remain cached, including absent keys. Listeners and queried DOM references belong to a menu-visible DisposableStore and are cleared on close or control disposal. No new long-lived collection or network cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in bounded added DOM work and unchanged storage/telemetry cardinality and lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact input-handler duration depends on surrounding browser invalidations; no independent expensive scaling mechanism was established for the small hit-test extension.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression. The option plumbing preserves workbench/Agents behavior, and the added query/rectangle fallback is bounded rather than collection-wide or retained.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag an editor/group, tree item, or external file after the last tab, including onto the add-tab button.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Drag feedback only resolves the target and updates indicator classes. On actual drop, the existing onDrop transfer branch moves/copies editors or extracts resources and opens them. External drops await extraction, host focus, trust/resolution, and grouped opening; none runs merely from hovering over the button.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract dropped browser files through filesystem handles, or read accepted fallback File objects into memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction per actual external drop; at most one handle acquisition or fallback FileReader per dropped file. Existing fallback skips files larger than 100 MB. No per-tab calls. The added button target uses the same handler as empty strip space.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Drops on the button were ignored; equivalent after-last-tab drops on empty strip space already used this exact extraction path and file cardinality. The diff expands the explicit drop target without adding duplicated processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction is awaited before opening dropped resources, but never by drag feedback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist web filesystem handles through the existing optional IndexedDB registration path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by handles in the explicit drop and existing handle-map reuse. File-transfer extraction starts items concurrently and joins them with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary occurred for the same files dropped on empty strip space; the button now accepts that operation too.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Handle registration is awaited as part of browser drop extraction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus the host window and optionally add one batch of external local resources to the recent list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One focus call and at most one recent-list batch per actual external-resource drop, independent of the number of open tabs. Workspace probing is disabled by allowWorkspaceOpen:false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No action on the button itself; identical existing boundary calls for an equivalent drop on empty strip space.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host focus is awaited; the recent-list call is not awaited here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse transferred URI data and resolve/open dropped editor inputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Tree transfer IDs are extracted sequentially, then passed to one openEditors call. EditorService resolves candidates in its existing loop, groups by destination, and submits one group.openEditors per destination group rather than one boundary call per open tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transfer, resolution, and grouped-open implementation handled existing tab/empty-strip targets. Only acceptance of the button target changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transfer data and editor resolution precede completed opening. Provider/model loading remains the existing editor-service responsibility.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Editors/files/transfer IDs in one deliberate drop, not tab count or drag-event frequency. Existing local group/editor transfers bypass external extraction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Feedback is synchronous and bounded. Local editor moves/copies iterate their transfer list. Tree transfers await each transfer ID. Browser file extraction uses Promise.all; editor input resolution is sequential before destination-group opens are joined. These patterns are inherited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Drop feedback deduplicates unchanged left/right target elements. Local transfer stores are cleared after handling. Downstream filesystem-handle and editor/model reuse are unchanged; there is no new retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff only extends the target and fixes indicator ownership; all expensive work remains behind one actual drop and retains its previous batching/concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External file sizes, provider latency, and contributed editor behavior vary, but this diff does not increase processing cardinality for the same logical drop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Newly accepted button drops necessarily reach the established after-last-tab workflow; hover feedback does not fan out into extraction or opening, and no duplicate drop invocation was found.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 14 changed files and all diff pages against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. Submitted one low-severity, high-confidence finding for repeatedly undoing/reapplying the followed tab layout on warm geometry-neutral updates. Reviewed menu input/lifecycle, explicit recent-first option propagation, drag/drop boundaries and grouping, CSS changes, and tests/fixtures. No concrete old performance-regression fix with qualifying provenance was identified; the other fixes address layout/interaction correctness.
